# Modular weapon animations — firing / payload / impact

**Implemented subsystem, not yet a desktop/Android visual acceptance.** No new art is required or generated by this system. It composes existing, atlas-derived textures into three separately timed components. The previous synthetic-pill animation batch is NOT used.

## Runtime contract

| Stage | Starts when | Attached to | Ends when | Source art |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1. FIRING** | Simulation authorizes a weapon shot | Source ship's actual registered origin (currently ship center in `Battle`) | Its own one-shot frame count expires | `effects/weapon_fx/<type>/firing_01.png` onward |
| **2. PAYLOAD** | Same shot launches | Actual moving missile or transient beam; re-sampled every tick | Simulation removes the projectile/beam | Existing curated `effects/beams/{blue,gold,red,violet}_01..07.png`; optional per-missile `effects/weapon_fx/<type>/payload_01.png` |
| **3. IMPACT** | Simulation resolves a genuine hit | World-space contact position | Its own one-shot sequence fades | `effects/weapon_fx/<type>/impact_01.png` onward |

**Intercept** is a terminal variant of IMPACT, with its own optional frames. **Timeout/miss** never invents a successful impact animation. The three components can overlap, especially for instant-hit beams; stage durations do not alter simulation damage, reload, accuracy, targeting, guidance or velocity.

`Battle.VisualEvent` is an append-only, bounded **sequence-numbered history** with `FIRE`, `IMPACT`, `INTERCEPT` and `TIMEOUT` outcomes, shot identity, simulation tick, weapon kind, source/target IDs, and world positions. Every physical beam and missile carries a stable `visualId` and `spawnTick`. Multi-step catchup between rendered frames does not discard events immediately. No renderer is allowed to call hit, damage, fire, spawn projectile or consume ammo.

The renderer `ModularWeaponFxRenderer` tracks seen event IDs, instantiates one-shot muzzle and impact clips, and renders live payloads using **real** `Battle.Beam` and `Battle.Missile` positions. Missing art skips only the missing visual stage and retains prior working fallback line/circle drawing; it never replaces real art with a new fabricated shape. All PNG texture instances are cached and disposed. `WeaponBeamSprites` now samples its texture animation relative to each shot's spawn tick, not global elapsed time.

## First supplied art mapping (existing graphics only)

The package **`Catastrophic_Diplomacy_Modular_FX_Existing_Art.zip`**, preserved in the Catastrophic Diplomacy Library, contains 63 source-cropped firing and impact frames plus the 35 existing curated payload beam strips. The first four working families are:

| Kind | FIRING source atlas / row | PAYLOAD source | IMPACT source atlas / row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Laser (blue) | `blue_sci_fi_energy_vfx_sprite_sheet.png` / 1 | existing blue beam strips | same blue atlas / 3 |
| Kinetic (gold) | `golden_sci_fi_energy_vfx_sprite_sheet.png` / 1 | existing gold beam strips | same gold atlas / 3 |
| Plasma (crimson) | `crimson_energy_slash_vfx_atlas.png` / 1, frames 1–7 | existing **red** beam strips | same crimson atlas / 3 |
| Particle (violet) | `purple_energy_vfx_sprite_sheet.png` / 1 | existing violet beam strips | same violet atlas / 3 |

Original artwork is an **eight-column, three-row, 1774×887 RGBA atlas**. The row identities are *source-level art conventions* selected for first-pass curation, not permission to automatically accept arbitrary generated sheets. Cropping preserves source pixel provenance, adjusts dark matte contamination using alpha only, and rejects high-intensity content along frame boundaries (>2.5% of an eight-pixel border). The eighth crimson FIRING cell and the separate cyan/triple-beam sheets were held back rather than allowing suspect crops into the runtime pack. The extraction source/checksums and an on-checkerboard review sheet are included in the ZIP.

These 98 images are **not new concepts**, and the ZIP is intended to be unpacked at the repository root, preserving the `assets/effects/...` paths. The binary PNGs are backed up in the Library transfer pack, but **not claimed to be committed to GitHub**. If you use the ZIP, re-run the application to refresh its texture cache. The bundled package is a functional art handoff, not proof that a particular desktop or APK build contains the files.

## Future module weapon compositions (no new images needed)

`WeaponFxProfile` supplies a profile per weapon type. A profile contains separate `Clip` descriptors (asset path, frame count, ticks per frame, looping rule, world dimensions) for firing, payload, impact and optional intercept variant. The same firing effect can be combined with a different missile body or shield-hit art without having to render whole fake weapon animations. Existing atlas snippets can be reassigned to other profiles by changing mapping metadata; no physical emitter must appear in any FX sprite.

Additional weapon types can use the same approach:
- Missile: hatch/muzzle flash → physically guided missile texture → explosion or distinct interception burst
- Torpedo: heavy launch bloom → slow physically guided torpedo body → large impact bloom
- Point defense: short muzzle arc → tracer or brief beam → small intercept flash
- Flak: combustion muzzle → traveling shell → spatially expanding fragmentation burst
- Fighter/drone: launch effect → existing craft renderer → hit/intercept/return effect

**Current boundary:** Only the four primary beam families have source-cropped firing/impact art mapped in the supplied ZIP. Missile, torpedo, fighter, drone, PD and flak can already emit or consume some runtime events, but do not yet have all three individually curated visual clips. There is no pre-fire anticipation event; the first FIRING frame begins the shot tick. The muzzle event location currently follows the underlying combat origin, which is ship center; faction-specific physical socket anchors will be a separate source-of-truth integration with `HullLayouts`. Impact coordinates are at the target center/contact region according to current simulation, not a detailed surface collider yet.

## Acceptance and regression checklist

1. Install ZIP at repo root, verify hashes in `assets/effects/weapon_fx/extraction_manifest.json`; check the on-checkerboard contact sheet.
2. Execute `gradle :core:weaponFxSmoke` (also chained into existing combat smoke). This tests frame sampler bounds, per-shot visual event IDs, real missile impact, deterministic simulation replay, and separate firing vs impact notifications. It **does not** test artistic quality.
3. Launch `gradle :desktop:run`; observe that a weapon has (a) source flash, (b) correct live payload, (c) target impact. Capture the video in the static weapon firing range. Do not claim this ran unless it did.
4. Review each frame and all seams, muzzle alignment, impact positions, texture cleanup, overdraw, delayed impact vs immediate beam and 1× time; fix only failed assets/behaviors. Never approve visual art from file hashes alone.
5. Verify Android asset inclusion after full Git binary ingestion, profile-dependent texture availability, 200v200 cap behavior and GL30/fallback paths.

### Source files
- Core event source: `core/src/main/java/diplomacy/sim/Battle.java`
- Profile configuration: `core/src/main/java/diplomacy/fx/WeaponFxProfile.java`
- Graphics composer: `game/src/main/java/diplomacy/client/ModularWeaponFxRenderer.java`
- Beam payload: `game/src/main/java/diplomacy/client/WeaponBeamSprites.java`
- Integration: `game/src/main/java/diplomacy/client/CatastrophicGame.java`
- Regression test: `core/src/test/java/diplomacy/sim/WeaponFxPipelineTest.java`

This is intentionally modular and independent of whether a specific effect uses a beam, orb, bullet, torpedo or homing missile. The physics always decides what happened; the visuals are authored compositions of three effects triggered by that decision.

## Shared combat lighting and exhaust (desktop / Android / battle screensaver)

`game/src/main/java/diplomacy/client/CombatLightingRenderer.java` now shares the authoritative battle/world camera with the existing three-stage weapon composer. Its additive radial falloff pass is applied **after real hull sprites, genuine beam art, projectiles and the GL2 geometry fallback**. Consequently the local bloom brightens nearby hull pixels rather than drawing an unrelated HUD overlay. The emissive pass renders:

- Facing- and speed-dependent engine nozzle lights and thrust cones for either ship renderer, with dim idle light.
- Two-layer colored beam coronas and endpoint glow for **live** simulation beams, including fallback lines if beam textures are absent.
- Separate simulation event-driven firing, impact and interception blooms; large kinetic shots receive stronger/longer muzzle illumination. TIMEOUT creates no explosion.
- Illuminated guided missile/torpedo exhaust **only after cold-launch ignition**, attached to current projectile velocity and position.
- Intentionally stylized smoke in vacuum, with sampled real missile positions, slight expansion, timed fading and short persistence after interception/impact.

`CombatLightingModel` is a pure Java, tick-driven and battle-scoped history. No additional combat events, hit/damage calculations or gameplay randomness are introduced. Repeated render frames at a paused tick do not spawn extra smoke or advance flashes. Cosmetic histories are bounded to 640 smoke elements, 384 event flashes and 192 tracked missiles; the renderer caps illuminated beam/missile bodies to 256/192 respectively and culls world-space quads against the battle camera. One 64×64 gradient texture is generated at initialization and reused for all glows, without per-light shader compilation, FBO allocation or texture lookup. Normal alpha blending is restored before the HUD.

**Quality boundary:** This is an efficient screen-space emissive illumination/bloom overlay, not normal-mapped shadow-casting light or a deferred light engine. The simulator's current FIRE event starts at the registered source-center; physical turret/nozzle sockets have not yet been introduced, so do not claim hardpoint-exact muzzle positioning. The original beam/hull artwork is preserved; this pass does not replace curated graphics or generate substitute ship sprites.

**Tests and evidence:** `gradle :game:lightingSmoke` exercises real missile launch and plume retention, deterministic pause behavior, bounded effect counts, timeout behavior and battle replacement. This task is also a dependency of the existing `:game:menuFlowSmoke` functional gate on Linux and Windows, without adding a workflow. The existing Android 200v200 emulator test now requires at least one actually rendered lighting quad and reports peak `glowQuads` and `smokeQuads` alongside existing weapon-art diagnostics. Its framebuffer screenshots are the visual-review starting point, not automatic proof that the lighting aesthetics, exposure or battery/performance budget are acceptable. Review live 1× speed, zoom levels, long beam volleys, cold launches, huge kinetic salvos and 200v200 frame times on hardware before art sign-off.

## Restored original modular weapon sprites (October 30, 2026)

The original `Catastrophic_Diplomacy_Modular_FX_Existing_Art.zip` was
retrieved from the project Library, inspected as a 2160×858 checkerboard
contact sheet, and byte-verified against its embedded frame/payload manifest.
The exact original 6,503,142-byte archive (SHA-256
`1d65ce25dbe0fb4fccf0f85b6054fadf380b7ab8aaff3a9ce9129a39bcbf338a`)
is now represented as twenty **base64 transport chunks** under
`asset_packs/weapon-fx/`. `prepareModularWeaponFx` reconstructs it,
verifies its original full-archive SHA-256, manifest inventory, each PNG
SHA-256 and PNG signature, then stages **63 original firing/impact sprites**
into `effects/weapon_fx/`. The **35 original beam strips** remain sourced
from the already-committed, separately validated stage-1 runtime pack.
Both Android asset merge and desktop asset staging require this new task.

The weapon composer now actually finds its laser, kinetic, plasma and particle
firing/impact frames in normal distributions, rather than silently skipping
these optional textures. Kinetic shells also use an authored, time-relative
gold tracer strip as a render-only payload when a dedicated physical shell
sprite is absent; the collision-tested shell position remains authoritative.

**Not yet art-approved:** These images passed source-hash and preliminary
contact-sheet checks, not a completed in-game frame-by-frame aesthetic QA.
Guided missile/torpedo **bodies**, flak, dedicated point-defense flashes,
fighter and drone launch art still need source review and correct individual
runtime sprites. Do not repurpose a UI missile glyph or entire arsenal
sheet as a missile. Debug geometry is retained ONLY when the corresponding
real art is missing, while the lighting/exhaust pass remains active.
